answer.rationale: Incumbent already refused a price reopen and an 18% spend cut is mandated, so renew or a further negotiate attempt is unlikely to minimize TCO. The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew; deferral (c5) was only shown safe for non-critical month-to-month service and would raise delivery risk on a 94% loaded line with no buffer. Adding a second source does not replace the expiring primary. c2 is the only inherited path that cut unit cost with reportedly quick onboarding; c1 is the counter-record on incumbent stability. Those two archives must be checked before any commitment. Even if c2 holds, the timeline and utilization imply downstream disruption risk, so any switch stays a small guarded test rather than a broad cutover.
